open_points.subject: open_store validation ordering
open_points.text: open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on a lock file inside data_directory, opened without following links and held for the life of the process; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, the file opened without following links; create its tables with create_store_schema, which leaves existing tables as they are; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue and no file fixture record names, which is a digest for which list_stored_value_rows_by_value_digest answers no row, and create the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.
open_points.other_text: open_store: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError whose reason names the failed check: data_directory does not exist (it is never created here), lock held by another process, directory not private (naming the first offending path), or symbolic link found (naming its path); it removes and creates nothing when a check fails.
open_points.question: Must the lock file be created before the privacy and symbolic-link checks, or must those checks occur before anything is created so their failure creates nothing?

open_points.subject: open_store orphan cleanup
open_points.text: open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on a lock file inside data_directory, opened without following links and held for the life of the process; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, the file opened without following links; create its tables with create_store_schema, which leaves existing tables as they are; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue and no file fixture record names, which is a digest for which list_stored_value_rows_by_value_digest answers no row, and create the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.
open_points.other_text: - RecordType enum values: 'slot', 'contract_version', 'implementation', 'trial_case', 'trial_execution', 'admission_verdict', 'activation', 'binding', 'flow', 'flow_version', 'flow_activation', 'run', 'node_execution', 'stored_value', 'spooled_file', 'approval', 'grant', 'effect_attempt'; Python member names were not available in models context.
open_points.question: Must the cleanup rule stop referring to a file fixture record, or must such a record type and its repository access be added to the prompt?

open_points.subject: page_records whole-type listing
open_points.text: page_records: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the rows of record_type in store order through StoreRepository and never ask the database for a limit, a range or a set condition: with no filter the type's whole list (list_slot_rows for slots, list_run_rows for runs, and so for every listed type); with an equals filter the type's equality list of the named field (list_run_rows_by_status, list_node_execution_rows_by_run_id, and for node executions list_node_execution_rows_by_executed_implementation_id for executed_implementation and list_node_execution_rows_by_executed_binding_id for executed_binding), a status value passed as the member of the type's status enumeration; with an in_set filter one such list per value, merged by store_position without repeating a row; it then reverses that order, keeps the rows whose store_position is below the token's position, and returns the records of the first page_size of them.
open_points.question: Must page_records exclude stored values from unfiltered paging, or must StoreRepository provide the required whole-list operation for StoredValue rows?

open_points.subject: page_records continuation-position validation
open_points.text: page_records: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise InvalidRequestError when decode_continuation_token refuses the token or when the position it names is not the position of a record of record_type, which is a position for which the type's find operation at that position (find_run_row_at_position for runs, and so for every listed type) answers no row, whether or not that record still matches record_filter; allowed fields, the number of conditions and page_size are checked by the caller and not again here.

open_points.subject: record_change mutable fields
open_points.text: record_change: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] Content records and trace records (contract versions, implementations, trial cases, trial executions, admission verdicts, activations, flow versions, flow activations, stored values, node executions, spooled files) are never updated or deleted once written; only the status and decision fields of Run, OperationBinding, EffectApproval, StandingGrant and EffectAttempt records change, and only through record_change.
open_points.other_text: record_change: [BEHAVIOR] MUST apply the one StoreChange given in one SQLite transaction that either writes every record the variant lists or nothing; it writes no record the variant does not list and trusts the caller for every decision of the caller's rule, checking only its own invariants: attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, existing linked records, and no edit of an immutable record. Records of the kinds that are never edited — issued contract versions, implementations, trial cases, flow versions, values, verdicts, activations and trace records — are only ever written once; for any other entity a lifecycle change — a status, who decided, resolved, revoked, cancelled or released and when, concluded_at, ended_at, waiting points, outputs — updates those fields of the entity's one record in place, and the record keeps its store position, the position of its creation; no other field of a written record ever changes.
open_points.question: Are mutable records limited to status and decision fields, or may record_change also update concluded_at, ended_at, waiting points, outputs and the other lifecycle fields listed here?

open_points.subject: record_change returned record fields
open_points.text: record_change: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns a RecordSet holding every record the change wrote or changed, each with every identity, store position, attempt_number and by-field the module assigned.
open_points.other_text: - Slot fields (exact, no others exist): slot_id: str, purpose: str, created_by: Actor, created_at: KernelInstant
open_points.question: Must store_position be returned only in row metadata or only for record models that declare it, or must models such as Slot gain a store_position field?
